key_insight: Perceive-to-Reason (P2R) separates “finding the right visual evidence” from “reasoning over that evidence,” making fine-grained visual reasoning more reliable on high-resolution images. Instead of mixing perception and reasoning, the model uses a two-stage pipeline to first detect small critical cues and then answer using those cues.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the difficulty vision-language models have with fine-grained visual reasoning when important details are tiny, scattered, or buried in large high-resolution images. Existing methods often use repeated cropping or visual search, but they do not explicitly decouple perception from reasoning.
method: Formulates fine-grained visual reasoning as a two-stage process: perceive first, reason second.
Uses a perception stage to identify or extract the most relevant local visual evidence from large images.
Feeds the selected evidence into a reasoning stage to generate the final answer, reducing distraction from irrelevant regions.
impact: This approach can improve accuracy and robustness on tasks that depend on subtle visual details, such as document understanding, medical imaging, remote sensing, and complex scene analysis. For practitioners, it offers a cleaner framework for building interpretable vision-language systems that handle high-resolution inputs more effectively.

paper_title: Perceive-to-Reason: Decoupling Perception and Reasoning for Fine-Grained Visual Reasoning
paper_authors: Hongxing Li, Xiufeng Huang, Dingming Li, Wenjing Jiang, Zixuan Wang
